issues.description: Constructors for Animal-derived classes (Seal, Pig, Goat) are inconsistent between artifacts: the template's example instantiations in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java use two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the UML/problem statement and the solution implementation define Animal with a single attribute name and use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and whether an additional attribute is expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent: update the commented example instantiations in template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use single-argument constructors that pass only the name (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML and solution. Alternatively, if the exercise intends additional attributes (e.g., type/habitat), update the UML/problem statement and solution classes to include those fields and adjust constructors and examples accordingly.
